text:
elena: Thinking about tightening our scale-out triggers for spot-backed inference. Proposal: quantile-driven triggers + soft-hedge to on-demand instead of instant hard swap. Want feedback on cooldowns / surge caps.

samir: Love quantiles. Which metrics are we considering? p95 latency? pending_reqs per GPU?

elena: p95 + queue_wait_p95 (95th percentile of time a request sits in the batch queue). Also weight decisions by spot_interruption_rate per AZ. Trigger when p95 > 120ms OR queue_wait_p95 > 250ms for 3 consecutive 30s windows (to avoid noise).

phil: 3x30s windows (~90s) sounds reasonable. For cooldowns, suggest scale_up_cooldown = 120s and scale_down_cooldown = 300s. We should cap surge to avoid cost runaway — max_surge 15% of target GPU capacity and a burst budget (GPU-minutes/hr).

ravi: +1. Also prefer a "soft_hedge" behavior: bring up on-demand slowly instead of replacing all spot. Eg: initial hedge 10% on-demand, if interruptions continue escalate every 3m by +15% up to 25%. This limits cost shock and keeps spot footprint non-zero.

elena: Also plan to use a small warm-standby pool in alternate AZs (cross-AZ hedging). Important: prewarm KV cache and model weights on warm nodes to avoid latency cliffs when they take traffic.

samir: Example config sketch: 
```
autoscaler:
  mode: mixed_spot
  triggers:
    - metric: p95_latency_ms
      threshold: 120
      window: 30s
      consecutive: 3
    - metric: queue_wait_p95_ms
      threshold: 250
      window: 30s
      consecutive: 3
  scale_cooldown: 120s
  scale_down_cooldown: 300s
  max_surge: 0.15
  soft_hedge:
    initial: 0.10
    step: 0.15
    step_interval: 180s
  burst_budget_gpu_minutes_per_hour: 120
```

phil: Couple of guards to add: 1) gate hedging by interruption_probability (only trigger if > 0.02 for the pool) and 2) respect spot_pool_occupancy < 0.85 before trying to scale more spot. Prevents pointless churn.

ravi: Also add smoothing rules to avoid oscillation: exponential backoff on scale-down amplitude, and require stable q50/q75 below thresholds for 5m before reducing capacity.

infra-bot: Heads up: cloud providers differ on preemption notice (GCP ~30s, AWS spot termination ~2m). Our hedging windows should be provider-aware — don't rely on a single fixed cooldown.

elena: :thumbsup: Can someone run a sim over historical traces (Dec–Jan traffic) and estimate cost delta vs current baseline? Target: < +7% cost increase for improved tail stability; ideally < +3%. If we cannot meet cost target, tighten surge caps.

samir: I'll run the sim and include region-aware preemption traces. Quick Q: do we also want to reject low-priority requests when surge budget is exhausted? I propose token-bucket per-customer + degrade to cheaper quantized model or cached response.

phil: Yes — degrade paths should be first-class: cached embeddings, lower-precision model variant, or serve from cached prefix (if applicable) before hedging to on-demand.

deploy-bot: autoscaler-config:hybrid-quantile-v1 applied to staging at 2035123468 by elena — dry-run only, no scale actions observed.

ravi: If staging looks good, plan canary to us-west-2 at 02:00 UTC with 10% of traffic and active telemetry on p95, queue_wait_p95, interruption_rate, and cost burn.

samir: I'll attach sim results in a follow-up thread + a short CSV of hourly GPU-minutes and p95 deltas.

elena: Thanks all — goal is predictable tail latency with controlled cost. I'll open an RFC doc after we get sim numbers.
